results.title: Harmonizing foundation models in healthcare
results.content: # Harmonizing foundation models in healthcare: A comprehensive survey of their roles, relationships, and impact in artificial intelligence’s advancing terrain. Foundation models improve healthcare by integrating medical data. Advances in explainable AI and interoperability will improve trust and accessibility. Collaboration among AI developers, healthcare experts, and policymakers is essential. The lightning development of artificial intelligence (AI) has revolutionized healthcare, helping significant improvements in various applications. This paper provides a comprehensive review of foundation models in healthcare, highlighting their transformative potential in areas such as diagnostics, personalized treatment, and operational efficiency. Regardless their assurance, difficulties remain, including data privacy concerns, bias in AI algorithms, and the need for extensive computational resources. Our analysis identifies emerging trends and future directions, emphasizing the importance of ethical AI deployment, improved interoperability over healthcare systems, and the development of more robust, domain-specific models. Future research should focus on enhancing model interpretability, ensuring equitable access, and fostering collaboration between AI developers and healthcare professionals to maximize the advantages of these technologies.

results.content: As one industry expert put it, _"the integration of data science in drug discovery is evolving beyond mere trial phases to practical uses – especially in the creation and testing of molecular compounds **in silico**."_ Algorithms simulating biological interactions can **significantly accelerate drug discovery**, improving the efficiency of initial testing and opening doors to novel therapies ([[13]](https://pharmaphorum.com/digital/how-data-science-and-ai-will-transform-life-sciences-2025#:~:text=,world%20solutions "Highlights: ,world solutions")). They ensure data from labs, trials, [EHRs](https://intuitionlabs.ai/articles/electronic-patient-record-systems), etc., flows into analytics platforms in a usable, secure form ([[47]](https://www.csgtalent.com/insights/blog/essential-data-science-roles-in-life-sciences-for-2024/#:~:text=Data%20Architect "Highlights: Data Architect")). **Sources:** The information in this article is derived from a range of 2024–2026 industry reports, expert analyses, and case studies, including Deloitte's 2025 life sciences outlook ([[81]](https://www.deloitte.com/us/en/insights/industry/health-care/life-sciences-and-health-care-industry-outlooks/2025-life-sciences-executive-outlook.html)), pharmaphorum's predictions for AI in 2025 ([[82]](https://pharmaphorum.com/digital/how-data-science-and-ai-will-transform-life-sciences-2025)), ZS Associates' life sciences tech survey ([[83]](https://www.zs.com/insights/2025-survey-data-digital-ai)), FDA's January 2025 AI guidance ([[29]](https://www.fda.gov/regulatory-information/search-fda-guidance-documents/considerations-use-artificial-intelligence-support-regulatory-decision-making-drug-and-biological)), EMA's AI reflection paper ([[32]](https://www.ema.europa.eu/en/news/reflection-paper-use-artificial-intelligence-lifecycle-medicines)), Insilico Medicine's Phase IIa results in Nature Medicine ([[15]](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41591-025-03743-2)), the Recursion-Exscientia merger announcement ([[78]](https://ir.recursion.com/news-releases/news-release-details/recursion-and-exscientia-two-leaders-ai-drug-discovery-space)), Siemens' Dotmatics acquisition ([[79]](https://news.siemens.com/en-us/dotmatics-closing/)), and market analysis from Global Market Insights ([[2]](https://www.gminsights.com/industry-analysis/ai-in-drug-discovery-market)), among other sources.
